resolutions: The capability spec now states the factory-required why, behaviour, and testable acceptance criteria while retaining the approved detailed design.
The design keeps MCP and skill sources separate from durable semantic-capability authority.
The Web surface uses same-origin session facades and does not expose Control API Bearer credentials.
The first release has no hard agent delete or configuration-version restore.
current_flow: Current main has fixture-backed Agents routes, unpaginated Control API agent listing, versioned profile files, source/capability replacement, and no browser management facade or custom-role domain.

criteria_map.Truthful directory and role library: Adds server-owned browser projections and paginated contracts rather than extending fixture data.
criteria_map.Separated agent setup: Creates the base agent before independently saved source and capability revisions.
criteria_map.Authority boundary: Reuses the existing source versus semantic-capability lifecycle; raw MCP tools are never stored as authority.
criteria_map.Secure browser operation: Browser routes use session authentication, administrator mutation authorization, Origin and CSRF checks, and sanitized DTOs.
criteria_map.Accessible functional UI: Every visible control maps to a route, observable view state, or browser-facade operation with tested states.

new_abstractions: One app-scoped custom-role template domain/application contract is required; no parallel agent-access or browser-auth model is introduced.

citations.finding: MCP source attachment cannot imply action authority.
Removing an agent is disable-and-preserve, not hard delete.
Browser sessions and bearer Control API credentials are separate trust paths.
